articles.headline: Appeal of the Trustees of the A.M.E. Book Concern of Philadelphia
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: Appeal to the bishops and ministers announcing that after nearly fifty years the Church has purchased a house and lot for its Book Concern and paper at No. 631 Pine street, Philadelphia (near the present office), having borrowed money for the first payment; asks $4,000 by the 25th of April 1866. Signed by the committee. Note: the Book Depository advertisement on p.4 still prints the old address, No. 619 Pine street.

articles.headline: Sketches of our Bishops
articles.summary: Biographical sketches of Bishop William Paul Quinn (senior bishop, then at the Ohio Annual Conference) and Bishop D. A. Payne, D.D. (born Charleston S.C.; studied at Gettysburg Seminary under Dr. Schmucker; only colored clergyman in the country to hold the degree of Doctor of Divinity; President of Wilberforce College). An 'Apology' on p.2 regrets it could not get fuller facts.

articles.headline: Important Letter from Bishop Campbell
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Bishop Campbell forwards an article clipped from the Southern Advocate (Macon, Ga.) and urges that the A.M.E. Church must have immediately a thoroughly educated ministry in numbers equal to the demands of the South. A second signed missionary letter by J. P. Campbell appears on p.1 col.7 calling for more men for the missionary field. Southern-missions / migration topic.

articles.headline: What High-Toned Men Think (streetcar exclusion)
articles.summary: Recalls that two weeks ago the paper published the touching letter of Mrs. Frances Ellen Harper, the eminent lecturer, to one of the city papers, complaining of exclusion from a city railroad car on account of her color. The National Baptist, a religious journal published in this city, condemned the 'foul outrage upon Mrs. Harper' as a relic of barbarism, noting that clean, well-behaved black passengers are put off the street cars of this city. Streetcar-exclusion topic.
people: lecturer, excluded from a Philadelphia city railroad car

articles.headline: News from the Churches -- Rev. Thomas Cooper
articles.summary: Rev. Thomas Cooper, pastor of A.M.E. Church, Trenton, N.J., has been very ill for near two months; it was determined by the Preachers' Meeting held in this city (Philadelphia) to go up and visit him. Same column: Sister Louisa Dixon, an esteemed member of Bethel Church, Baltimore (Rev. S. L. Hammond, pastor), a widow, sent her pastor $3.00 as a Semi-Centenary gift -- thought to be the first given. (Dixon and Hammond are Baltimore, text only.) Semi-Centenary topic.
people: pastor, A.M.E. Trenton N.J. (Rev.); visited by the Philadelphia Preachers' Meeting

articles.headline: Personal Items
articles.summary: Local personal notes: Bishop James P. Campbell has been heard from since leaving for the West. Rev. W. D. W. Schureman was in Philadelphia last week and returned to Baltimore last Saturday, having come to perform a marriage ceremony. Rev. Edward Hammond of Ashmun Institute spent Saturday and Sabbath last in this city. Rev. J. D. Brooks, superintendent of an A.M.E. Zion Church, was heard last Sabbath night at Wesley church on Lombard St. (Big Wesley). Miss Jane M. Lynch arrived from Charleston en route to Baltimore, transferred by the National Freedmen's Relief Association as a teacher.
people: in Philadelphia to perform a marriage (Rev.)

articles.headline: Local Items -- Easter (Religious) Services and Bethel Trustee Election
articles.summary: Easter Sunday services: Bethel Church (Rev. Wm. Moore, pastor) -- the pastor preached on the Resurrection and administered the Sacrament; at 3 P.M. Rev. Stephen Smith preached, at 7.30 P.M. Rev. E. Weaver preached. Union Church, 3 P.M., densely crowded, Rev. R. P. Gibbs pastor preached (Text Matthew 28:6, Tomb of Jesus). Pearl St. Baptist Church (Rev. T. D. Miller, pastor) saw a large Easter baptism and reception of some twelve members, one a young white lady; quarterly union meeting of the Baptist churches of this vicinity to meet there next Sunday. Election of Trustees at Bethel Church last Monday night: terms of Messrs. Theodore Young, Joshua Kelly and (--) Wilson expired; chosen in their places Messrs. Peter D. Lewis, John Van Brockle and Arthur Tate. A company of 'solid' colored men of this city are converting the old High School building on Lombard Street into a large hall with stores beneath, shares $1,000 each, with Messrs. Smith, Whipper and Weaver among the stockholders. Festivals in progress at Brick Wesley and Little Wesley churches.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: Three marriages: March 25, by Geo. T. Waters, Mr. Samuel Blackston to Miss Ann Molleton, both of Smyrna, Del.; March 22, by Rev. John Peck, H. Lee of Oberlin, Ohio, and Miss Haddessah R. Moles of Pittsburgh, Pa.; March 21, by Rev. Wm. M. Watson, Mr. Lorenzo F. Gould to Miss Margaret Steward, both of Gouldstown, N.J. (Smyrna and the Oberlin/Pittsburgh couple are out of area and kept to text.)

articles.headline: Died
articles.summary: Deaths (all out of the Philadelphia area, kept to text): Sister Violet Haley died 8 March 1866, aged 70 (Morristown, N.J.); Christopher Lavender, 54, killed in a steamboat collision on the Hudson, a member of the A.M.E. Church 20 years (Albany, N.Y.); and a correction from Wm. C. Hooper that his wife's name should read Ann Eliza Hooper, not Hopkins.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (Catharine Mason)
articles.author: Catharine Mason
articles.summary: A Philadelphia mother, Catharine Mason, at 1813 Hancock St., between Master and Thompson, Philadelphia, seeks her children Lewis, Lizzie and Kate, last seen in Owensboro', Ky., 'owned' by David and John Hart (the boy by Thomas Pointer). Dated March 31, 1866.
people: seeking her children; 1813 Hancock St., Philadelphia

articles.headline: African Civilization Society (advertisement)
articles.summary: Standing advertisement for the African Civilization Society. General Office: African Civilization Building, Dean St. near Troy Avenue, Brooklyn, N.Y.; Branch Offices No. 66 Sullivan St., New York, and F Street, Washington, D.C. Officers: President Rev. A. N. Freeman; Treasurer Jno. Peterson; Secretary Rev. H. M. Wilson; Assistant Secretary H. W. Bovall; General Superintendent of Schools and Gen'l Agent Rev. Rufus L. Perry, Washington, D.C. Incorporated under New York law to establish free schools for the Freedmen of the South; $1 annual subscription constitutes membership. All officers out of area (text only). Emigration/migration-and-freedmen topic; first appearance this quarter. (Standing ad; ran again May 5 and June 2, 1866, unchanged.)

articles.headline: Interesting Correspondence -- Ladies' Union Association and Gen. B. F. Butler
articles.author: Caira R. Le Count
articles.summary: Correspondence between the Corresponding Secretary of the Ladies' Union Association of this city (Philadelphia, for the benefit of sick and wounded colored soldiers) and Major-General B. F. Butler. From 604 Rodman Street, Philadelphia, Dec. 11, 1865, Caira R. Le Count (Cor. Sec.) notifies Butler that the Association, at its Fair, voted him ornaments (a sword) by 400 of 450 votes, to be given to Grant, Sherman, Sheridan or Butler. Butler's reply (Washington, March 19) thanks 'the Ladies of the Union Association, Philadelphia' through 'Carrie R. Le Count' and praises colored soldiers. Returning-soldiers / relief topic.

articles.headline: Our Semi-Centennial -- Philadelphia (Bethel immense meeting; Semi-Centenary Sunday)
articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA, PA. -- An immense meeting of the members of the A.M.E. Church of this city was held at Bethel Church (Rev. Wm. Moore, pastor) on Thursday evening, April 12th, the house literally packed. The pastor opened with divine service; Brother Abram Fields made the opening address, alluding to Bishop Allen. The original deeds of Bethel Church property (first ever held by the A.M.E. Church) were presented by brother Wilson: from R. Allen and wife to Richard Norris and others, Trustees, Oct. 10, 1791; Oct. 9, 1794; Oct. 11, 1817. A number of 'Semi-Centenary Members' who had belonged to Bethel nearly half a century sat before the altar; many had been of Bishop Allen's class, recalling when the only meeting-house was the old blacksmith shop at the corner of Sixth and Lombard. The widow of Rev. Jacob Tapsico (second ordained elder and second pastor of Bethel, appointed 1818) and the widow of Father Boggs (a founder) were present and spoke. Brother Lewis R. Seymour, a member over forty years, gave reminiscences of Bishop Allen (who kept a livery stable on Pine street, a grocery, and cows). Brother Fields proposed a Semi-Centenary Association. On Sunday the 15th at Bethel, Rt. Rev. Bishop Wayman preached in the forenoon, Rev. Wm. Moore in the afternoon, and Rev. Jas. Lynch at night; the church raised about $900 (Bethel to give about $1,400). Union A.M.E. (Rev. R. P. Gibbs pastor) raised $290 and expected $100 more (preaching by Bishop Wayman and Rev. James Lynch). Little Wesley A.M.E. (Hurst St., elder Rev. Jacob Mitchell) realized over $100. A.M.E. Semi-Centenary topic. (Out-of-area semi-centenary reports from Indianapolis, Ralston, Cincinnati kept to text.)
people: member over 40 years; Bishop Allen reminiscences

articles.headline: Our Semi-Centennial in the Sabbath Schools -- Bethel Sabbath School
articles.summary: The Sabbath School of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, celebrated the Semi-Centennial of the A.M.E. Church on Monday night (April 16). Admission fifteen cents. The meeting opened with prayer by the pastor, Rev. William Moore; exercises of Scripture recitations, dialogues and singing, and an address by the superintendent, W. C. Benton, on continuing the 'monument to Richard Allen.' The essay read by Miss Charlotte Scott showed superior ability; the Misses Allen and Maston distinguished themselves in singing; Mr. Shad was musical director; Anna Duff, a little girl, was the successful competitor (scholar giving the most money). The school expected to give not less than $200 to the Semi-Centennial Fund. A.M.E. Semi-Centenary topic.

articles.headline: Personal Items
articles.summary: Rev. Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward, arrived last Tuesday from the West (Ohio Conference). Rev. Bishop A. Wayman left this city Monday for Baltimore, having returned from the Ohio Conference. Rev. W. R. Revels is improving. Rev. Jas. A. Shorter (Ohio Conference) appointed agent for Wilberforce University. Rev. T. D. Miller, pastor of Pearl St. Baptist Church, is visiting Boston. Rev. Mr. Allston, rector of St. Thomas' Church, Philadelphia, preached at Wesley church, Lombard St. (Big Wesley), last Sunday evening. William A. Lynch, son of Rev. Benjamin Lynch, entered Ashmun Institute to fit for the ministry. Miss Jane M. Lynch (teacher, National Freedmen's Relief Association) appointed to Elkton, Md.
people: General Book Steward, returned from Ohio Conference (Rev.)
rector of St. Thomas' Church; preached at Big Wesley (Rev.)

articles.headline: A Misrepresentation -- defense of the Zion A.M.E. (Big Wesley)
articles.summary: A letter to the editor rebutting an article of March 24 ('On D.D.') that said the A.M.E. Zion Church is unable to support a pastor; the writers refer to the Minutes of the Philadelphia Annual Conference for the past three years and state they are not more than ten or twelve dollars in arrears, and call on the author to vindicate the Zion A.M.E. Church (Big Wesley, Lombard St.). Dated March 26, 1866. Signers below.

articles.headline: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- letter from Henry Highland Garnet
articles.author: Henry Highland Garnet
articles.summary: Published at the request of Mr. Jos. C. Bustill, Solicitor of the Equal Rights League: a letter (Washington, D.C., March 14, 1866) from Henry Highland Garnet to William Nesbit, Esq., President of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, praising the League's work and recalling the delegation that visited the Capital -- consisting of Nesbit, Wm. D. Forten and Jos. C. Bustill -- and their memorial to Congress for universal suffrage. Equal Rights League / suffrage topic. (Garnet and Nesbit out of area; the Philadelphia delegates linked.)
people: delegate, Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League

articles.summary: April 10th, by Rev. G. T. Waters, Mr. John Sanders to Miss Lydia Fraser, both of Kent (out of area; kept to text).

articles.summary: Little Virginia Augustine Parker died Feb. 9, 1866 after a long illness (notice by Miss M. A. Brown, out of area). H. articles.headline: Obituary
articles.summary: Died April 9, 1866, at the residence of Mr. Solomon Mahony, 1313 Pearl Street, Philadelphia, Catharine Winters, aged 87 years. Died April 18, James B. Hollowell, a worthy member, trustee and steward of the Union African M.E. Church, Coates Street, Philadelphia -- well beloved by both white and colored (notice by R. P. Gibbs). articles.headline: Great Union Intelligence Office (advertisement)
articles.summary: New advertisement (dated April 28, 1866): the Great Union Intelligence Office wants cooks, waiters, nurses, chambermaids, seamstresses and coachmen of all kinds; also men and women just from the South who wish to engage in farming can procure good homes by calling at the Office, No. 378 Washington Street. Good wages (up to $50 per month) paid to good servants. E. Demond & Co., No. 226 Washington St., Phila. (Employment/intelligence office serving colored servants and Southern freedpeople; freedmen/migration relevance.) (Standing ad; also ran May 19, 1866, where the proprietor is printed 'E. Demund & Co.')

articles.headline: The Day We Celebrate (semi-centenary)
articles.author: James A. Handy
articles.summary: A reflection urging the members and friends of the A.M.E. Church to assemble and celebrate their semi-centenary, dating the connection to Richard Allen fifty years before. Reviews the southern mission field (Wilmington, N.C., etc.) and reports Wilmington contributed sixty dollars. Signed James A. Handy, Supt. of Mission, North Carolina.

articles.headline: To the Enlisted Men of the Fourth U.S.C.T.
articles.author: G. M. Arnold
articles.summary: Farewell address to the discharged soldiers of the Fourth United States Colored Troops (styled Maryland's first colored heroes), recalling battles at Spring Hill, Petersburg, Dutch Gap, Deep Bottom, New Market Heights, Richmond and Fort Fisher, and naming commanding officers (Gen. Duncan, Cols. Rogers and Bornstein, Maj. Hill). Dated Washington, April 20, 1866.

articles.headline: To our Readers (editorial)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: Elisha Weaver explains that the present issue is less full than usual owing to the temporary absence of Editor Lynch and himself at the General Conference (Senate of the Church); promises matter on hand will be attended to in due time. Documents that Rev. James Lynch is the editor and Weaver the publisher.

articles.headline: Our Visit to the Baltimore Conference (editorial)
articles.author: E. W.
articles.summary: Elisha Weaver reports leaving Philadelphia in company with Rev. Stephen Smith for Washington, D.C., lodging at the Davis Hotel, and attending the Baltimore Annual Conference at Israel Church near Capitol Hill, all the bishops present. Notes the semi-centenary collections fell short of Bishop Payne's expectation; the proposed union of the A.M.E. Church and the A.M.E. Zion Connection was discussed and dismissed; and that in Washington colored persons are not excluded from riding in the cars (contrast with Philadelphia).

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: Four marriages reported. April 30, 1866, by Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, Mr. Samuel Rodney to Miss Sarah White, all of Philadelphia. April 17, by Rev. G. T. Waters, Robert Butcher to Matilda Loatman, all of Kent Co., Delaware. April 30, by Rev. Wm. Moore, Joseph C. Fisher of Columbia, Pa., to Mrs. Ann Maria Seekum of the same place. May 1, by the same, Isaac R. Evans of Salem, N.J., to Miss Margaret Moore of the same place.

articles.headline: Obituary -- Josiah Bond
articles.summary: Died on Sunday morning, 22d inst., in this city, Josiah Bond, in the 61st year of his age. Well known among the colored people of Philadelphia and the surrounding country; a plain working man of limited education who by self-study acquired knowledge of anti-slavery principles and labored zealously for the cause and the elevation of colored men. Visited the churches and sometimes officiated in their pulpits. Communicated (unsigned).

articles.headline: Information Wanted (notices)
articles.summary: A group of freedpeople's Information Wanted notices. One, by Joanna Whiters for her mother Carney Whiters (formerly of Elizabeth City, N.C.), directs replies to No. 707 Callowhill Street, Philadelphia. Another seeks George W. Burton (member of the 115th Regt. U.S. Colored Troops, last heard of at Brownsville, Texas, 1865), replies to his wife at No. 20 Acorn Alley, Philadelphia. Other notices (non-Philadelphia) seek Jane's children via W. A. Booream of Franklinton, N.C.; Gideon Johnson via Wesley Johnson of Pittsburg; Anderson Walker via Lucy Walker of Oswego, N.Y.; and the children of Mary Jones via their mother Larcenia Mayhoe (formerly of Nelson Co., Va.).

articles.headline: Sketches of our Bishops -- Bishop Jabez Pitt Campbell
articles.summary: Biographical sketch of Bishop Jabez Pitt Campbell. Born 1825 in Delaware of pious parents; joined the A.M.E. Church and was converted Christmas day 1825; in 1828 fled from Sussex Co., Delaware, to Pennsylvania to escape being seized and sold; was bound out by his father to Spencer Deweese, a merchant tailor in the city of Philadelphia, whom he served about four years, buying out the remainder of his time near the close of 1832; rejoined Bethel in Philadelphia, remaining a member of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, until 1839. Licensed to exhort by Bethel Church Quarterly Conference, Rev. Morris Brown pastor, July 1837; in 1838-39 supplied Bucks Co. Circuit, Pa., during the illness of the pastor Rev. Jeremiah Miller. Later: Conference Missionary of New England (under Noah C. Cannon), Providence, Albany, Buffalo, Flushing; appointed to Union Church, Philadelphia, 1854 (Editor and General Book Steward); elder in charge of Union Church, Phila., 1858; pastor of Bethel Church, Phila., 1862-63; elected and ordained bishop at the General Conference held at Philadelphia, May 1864.

articles.headline: Resolutions on the Christian Recorder / Rev. James Lynch appointed Editor
articles.summary: In the Baltimore Annual Conference report (read for the Recorder), Rev. James Lynch, Editor, urged the increased circulation of the Christian Recorder, calling it the organ of the A.M.E. Church and the people's paper; Bishop Payne and Chaplain Hunter pledged $5 each toward its circulation. Rev. J. M. Brown offered preamble and resolutions: Whereas the Recorder was resuscitated six years ago by Rev. Elisha Weaver and brought to high success, and whereas the joint office of General Book Steward and Editor was too onerous, Rev. James Lynch was appointed Editor, the division of labor proving conducive to the improvement of the church organ. Documents the Weaver-to-Lynch editorial transition.

articles.headline: William Whipper, Esq. (editorial notice)
articles.summary: Announces that 'our able, talented, and practical friend William Whipper, Esq., of Columbia, Pa.,' is writing a series of articles for the Christian Recorder, to appear over his own signature; Mr. Whipper, not the editor, is responsible for what he may say.

articles.headline: A.M.E. Semi-Centenary meetings (Washington, D.C.)
articles.summary: Under the heading 'A.M.E. Semi-Centenary,' two Washington accounts. (1) Semi-Centenary Meeting of Laymen at Israel Church, Washington, D.C., May 4; an immense audience, all bishops present; called to order by Brother George A. Hackett (a member 40 years), Bishop Quinn opening with prayer; addresses by J. L. Thomas of Union Bethel (Washington), W. E. Matthews of Baltimore, James Henry Jordan, and others; Captain A. P. Ketchum and John E. Hayes (editor, Savannah Republican) introduced. (2) From the Morning Chronicle: semi-centenary meeting at Union Bethel church (J. S. D. Hall, pastor), M street, Washington; prayer by Rev. H. W. Wilson. Also brief semi-centenary reports from Wilkesbarre, Pa. (W. H. Chase) and Cairo, Ill. (T. Strother). All named persons are non-Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: May 2, 1866, by Rev. G. K. Boyer, John Holt to Adaline Davis, both of Camden, N.J. May 2, by Rev. J. R. Hamilton, Henry Lane to Mrs. Elizabeth Jones, both of Princeton, N.J. On the 16th of May, by Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, Thomas Bracy to Miss Sarah Hotter, all of Philadelphia. May 8, by the Right Rev. articles.headline: Obituaries
articles.summary: Four deaths, none with a stated Philadelphia location: Mary Jane Briggs, daughter of Moses and Sarah A. Freeman, died March 14 in the second year of her age (no city stated); Peter Van Rensselaer, died Albany, N.Y., March 25, aged 45, member of the A.M.E. and later A.M.E. Zion Church; Amanda Lee, died Vicksburg, April 19, over twenty years a resident there; Zachariah Bridges, son of Rev. articles.headline: Information Wanted (notices)
articles.summary: Freedpeople's Information Wanted notices. The Philadelphia one: of my husband, George W. Burton, of Company A, 115th Regiment U.S. Army, last heard of in 1865 in the hospital at Brownsville; information to his wife, Jane Burton, No. 20 Acorn Alley, Philadelphia (chaplain R. R. articles.headline: Room to Rent for Societies -- Robert Jones (advertisement)
articles.summary: To Rent: a large furnished room suitable for the meetings of societies, at the S.E. corner Seventh and Market Sts. (fourth story). Apply to Robert Jones, No. 6 North 6th St., Philadelphia (new, dated May 12, 1866).

articles.headline: City items (editorial reports)
articles.summary: Local notices: Rev. Theodore D. Miller delivered an able lecture at Union church, Coates Street (Rev. J. P. Gibbs, pastor), on last Tuesday evening. There was a grand Sabbath School concert by the Pearl Street Baptist Sabbath School on last Thursday evening. Several candidates for admission to the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church were examined by the committee in the pastor's study at Bethel Church on Monday. (Also notes Miss Anna E. Dickinson, the white orator, lectured at the Academy of Music on May 20.) These confirm events announced in the May 19 issue.
people: lecturer at Union Church (Rev., pastor Pearl St. Baptist)
pastor of Union Church, Coates St. (Rev.)

articles.headline: Memorial of our Bishops -- to the M.E. Church South General Conference
articles.summary: The formal memorial of the A.M.E. bishops ('The African M.E. Church and the General Conference of M.E. Church South'), dated Baltimore, March 31, 1866, addressed to the bishops and clergy of the M.E. Church South in session at New Orleans, asking that houses of worship built by colored members in the South be peaceably transferred to the A.M.E. Church. Three ministers appointed to represent them: Rev. John Turner, Rev. Charles Burch, Rev. Henry M. Turner. Signed Daniel A. Payne, Alexander W. Wayman, Jabez P. Campbell, Bishops of the A.M.E. Church.

articles.headline: Information Wanted (notices)

articles.headline: Mrs. Sarah Irons -- shrouding and laying out of the dead (advertisement)
articles.summary: Shrouding and Laying Out of the Dead. Mrs. Sarah Irons (an old citizen of much experience) solicits the patronage of citizens and the public, being engaged in the business of shrouding and laying out the dead; terms moderate; she can always be found at No. 619 Pine Street, Philadelphia. (New ad, dated May 12, 1 year; also present in the May 19 issue.)

articles.headline: Second Session of the South Carolina Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church (reported)
articles.summary: Conference proceedings (Third and Fourth Days, Andrew's Chapel, Savannah, Ga., May 16-17, 1866), Bishop Payne presiding. Names the four bishops elected by the General Conference to superintend the A.M.E. Church; next session set for Wilmington, N.C., March 1867; District Book Repository to be located at Charleston, S.C. References Bishop D. A. Payne's book 'The Semi-Centenary and the Retrospection of the African Methodist Episcopal Church.' Rosters of southern local/itinerant preachers given in text (all non-Philadelphia).

articles.headline: W. Whipper on the Bishops' Address
articles.author: William Whipper
articles.summary: Letter to the editor criticizing the secular address of the Bishops of the A.M.E. Church to the 'Colored People of the United States.' Begins 'Sir:-You will please permit me to diverge from my former subject...' Signed William Whipper, Philadelphia, May 2[6], 1866. (Letter begins on p2 and concludes on p3 col 1.)

articles.headline: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League -- progress / Capital City Equal Rights Association (letter from Harrisburg)
articles.author: C. H.
articles.summary: Correspondence from Harrisburg reporting on a lecture under the auspices of the Capital City Equal Rights Association (auxiliary of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League). Notes the annual meeting of the State League approaching (2nd Wednesday in August 1866), with elections of officers and of representatives to the State League Convention. Signed 'C. H.,' Harrisburg, May 25th, 1866.

articles.headline: Public meeting for teachers and preachers for the Freedmen, Fourth Street Baptist Church, Philadelphia (quoted from The National Baptist)
articles.summary: Reprint from The National Baptist of a public meeting held at the Fourth Street Baptist Church, Philadelphia, a Sunday evening in April 1866, in behalf of teachers and preachers for the freedmen. Rev. Dr. Kennard presided; prayer and addresses by several Baptist ministers; Rev. L. A. Grimes of Boston, just returned from Virginia and North Carolina, presented facts. Resolution to form a society in each Baptist church in Philadelphia to aid the National Institute for Colored Preachers and Teachers for Freedmen.

articles.headline: A.M.E. Church, Germantown (church-funds lawsuit)
articles.author: A. B.
articles.summary: Statement of facts in the suit by the Trustees of the Bethel A.M.E. Church, Germantown, over Sewing-Circle/Fair funds. Money was deposited in the saving-fund in the names of James A. Nelson, his wife Catharine, and Sarah Hubert; the Trustees sued to recover control. Prints the court's decision (dated 520 Walnut Street, May 5, 1866, addressed to Wm. Richardson and other Trustees), holding the funds to be used only to pay the mortgage and to rebuild or repair the church. Signed 'A. B.'
people: co-holder of funds (wife of James A. Nelson)

articles.headline: Acknowledgments (subscription remittances received)
articles.summary: Standing column of subscription payments acknowledged from agents and subscribers across many states. articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: Married, on the 24th of May, by Rev. Jonathan B. Hamilton, Mr. Wm. J. Glover to Miss Lucy M. Custis, both of New Haven, Connecticut. (Couple non-Philadelphia; officiant not linked.)

articles.headline: A.M.E. Appointments, Sunday June 3; Bethel Sabbath School Anniversary and Missionary Meeting (notice)
articles.summary: Sunday (June 3) preaching appointments at the Philadelphia A.M.E. churches during the Conference session. Bethel Church (Ordination of Elders): 10 A.M. Rev. James A. Shorter, 3 P.M. Rev. Jonathan Hamilton, 8 P.M. Rev. G. Waters. Union Church: 10 A.M. Rev. W. H. Chase, 3 P.M. Rev. D. P. Seaton, 8 P.M. Bishop Wayman. Wesley Church: 10 A.M. Rev. R. Barney, 3 P.M. Rev. T. M. Kennard, 8 P.M. Rev. R. Fausset. Zion Mission, 7th below Dickerson: 10 A.M. Rev. A. Till, 3 P.M. (Ordination of deacons) Bishop Campbell, 8 P.M. Rev. Theo. Gould. Also: Sabbath School Anniversary at Bethel church, Monday June 4, 3 P.M.; Missionary Meeting at Bethel church, Tuesday June 5, 7:30 P.M.

articles.headline: South Carolina Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church (Second Session, continued; Fifth-Seventh Days)
articles.summary: Continuation of the South Carolina Annual Conference proceedings at Andrew's Chapel, Savannah, Ga. (Fifth through Seventh Days, May 18-20, 1866), Bishop Payne presiding; Secretary G. W. Brodie. Committees, ordinations and the southern stationings/appointments are given in full (all southern charges). The Conference was resolved into a Historical and Literary Society (Bishop Payne, President) and a Preacher's Aid Society (R. H. Cain, chair). Semi-Centenary collections for the District: for Missions, for Wilberforce University $91.01, for Book Concern, total about $281.77. An interview with Generals Steedman and Fullerton of the Freedmen's Bureau is recorded. Followed by a narrative 'The South Carolina Annual Conference' by Rev. H. M. Turner. (Continues the report begun June 2; recorded separately per owner's instruction.)
people: Superintendent of Missions, Southern division (Georgia); preacher in charge of Savannah mission; appointed special reporter for the Freedmen's Bureau interview (Rev.)

articles.headline: Personal Items
articles.summary: Church-news notes: a large number of ministers of the Philadelphia Annual Conference were in the city attending the Anniversaries; Bishop A. W. Wayman and wife spent the week in Philadelphia (an appeal that the A.M.E. churches buy a house for the Bishop); Bishop James P. Campbell expects to leave for the West in a few days; Rev. John M. Brown left Philadelphia for Baltimore last Wednesday; Rev. Thomas Kennard has removed from Canada to Philadelphia, his old home, joined the Philadelphia Annual Conference, and been appointed to a Pennsylvania charge.
people: removed from Canada to Philadelphia; joined the Philadelphia Conference (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice -- Hester Atkins, claimed niece of Rev. Richard Allen (Lunatic Hospital for Freedmen, Savannah)
articles.summary: Notice 'To all whom it may concern' from the Lunatic Hospital for Freedmen, Savannah, Ga., May 21, 1866: an old colored woman named Hester Atkins (the surname from her former owner, Mr. Atkins of S.C.) claims to be a niece of Rev. Richard Allen, formerly a Bishop of the A.M.E. Church, and says she was brought from the State of Pennsylvania when slavery existed there; her father's name was Anthony. Pastors of churches asked to take notice. Signed A. E. Augusta, M.D., Surgeon in charge 3d U.S.C.T.
people: named as her uncle; founding Bishop of the A.M.E. Church (Rev./Bishop)

articles.headline: Information Wanted -- Charles Watts
articles.summary: Charles Watts, who came to Philadelphia and is now living here, wishes to hear from his family, not seen for ten years: wife Jane and children Margaret, Drucilla, Elizabeth and Chas. Henry, last at Columbia, S.C. (when he was in the Rebel Army). Baptist ministers of Columbia, S.C., asked to inquire; information to Chas. Watts, care of R. A. Black, Christian Recorder Office, Philadelphia.
people: now living in Philadelphia; seeking his family

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: Includes: by Rev. J. Homer, Mr. John Drummond of Virginia to Miss Mary E. Ashton, of this city (Philadelphia); by Rev. W. R. Norris (May 19), Mr. Wm. Jackson of Germantown to Miss Dorcas A. Hopkins of Phoenixville, Chester Co., Pa.; by W. J. Davis (May 16, Lafayette, Ind.), John W. May of Springfield, Ill., to Olive Burch of Lafayette; and a batch by Rev. Henry Davis (Richard Broker to Sarah Thompson; Chas. Wm. Makee to Mary E. Hart; Andrew Jackson to Catharine M. Vinson; Cato Cisco to Susan Thompson; Joseph A. Arno to Mary E. Price, in New York) -- the Henry Davis marriages appear to be New York, non-Philadelphia.
people: bride, of Phoenixville, Chester Co., Pa.

articles.headline: Obituary
articles.summary: Nancy Holland, wife of Joseph Holland, departed this life at Coeymans, New York, May 10, 1866, aged 43, a longtime member of the A.M.E. Church (signed Leonard Patterson). Also: Elizabeth Talbot, died at Westville, Conn., May 20, of pneumonia, aged 58, daughter of Mary Fox and widow of the late John Lamon [VERIFY], of Philadelphia (signed Louisa Hope).

articles.headline: Editorial: a 'Headquarters' / Bishop's house for the A.M.E. Church in Philadelphia
articles.summary: Editorial arguing Philadelphia, as the cradle of the African Methodist Episcopal Church (its foundation stone laid here; the remains of 'the sainted Allen' repose under a plain marble slab in front of Bethel Church, Sixth St.), should have a 'Headquarters of the African Methodist Episcopal ministry' -- a house providing a residence for the presiding Bishop and lodging/reading rooms for visiting itinerant ministers. Notes the Church has four Bishops (two in the West within 75 miles of each other, two in the East within 100 miles), and cites Rev. James A. Shorter's sentiment. Proposes the Philadelphia Conference District fund it from the rent saved on the Bishop's house.
people: founder of the A.M.E. Church; his grave is at Bethel Church, Sixth St. (referenced)

articles.headline: William Moore's Bethel service; Rev. James Hollen's introductory sermon
articles.summary: Notes that William Moore has served Bethel church twice as pastor -- first in 1844-1846 [VERIFY first date], and lately, 1864-1866; the people hold him in honor; he is stationed at Trenton this year (where he served some time ago); growing in years but still vigorous, a student, progressive. Rev. James Hollen, the new pastor of Bethel church, preached his introductory discourse last Sunday morning (text: John i.27,28), making a very favorable impression.
people: served Bethel Church as pastor 1844-1846 and 1864-1866; now stationed at Trenton (Rev.)
new pastor of Bethel Church, Philadelphia; preached his introductory sermon (Rev.)

articles.headline: Personal Items
articles.summary: Bishop D. A. Payne, D.D., accompanied by Rev. James V. Simon [VERIFY], arrived in Philadelphia May 31 from Savannah, Ga. (his duties in the South Carolina Conference District); left June 2 for Baltimore. Mrs. William Beckart [VERIFY], Bishop Payne's mother-in-law, died at Georgetown, D.C., early last month, a devoted Roman Catholic. Bishop James P. Campbell has changed his residence from Carpenter St. to 1010 Addison St., Philadelphia. Rev. James Simms (Baptist, Savannah) arrived in Baltimore. Mrs. Frances E. W. Harper is at New London, Conn., lecturing to large audiences.
people: changed residence to 1010 Addison St., Philadelphia (Bishop)

articles.headline: Resolutions on the death of Jas. S. Hollowell (A.M.E. Union Church Sabbath school)
articles.summary: At a stated meeting of the teachers of the A.M.E. Union Church Sabbath school (Philadelphia), held Thursday evening April 18, 1866, the death of 'our late teacher,' Jas. S. Hollowell, was announced; a committee of three was appointed to draft resolutions of condolence. Preamble and resolutions adopted at the stated meeting of May 17 mourn Hollowell, 'known for his usefulness in the society in which he moved, and for his benevolence toward mankind.' Reported with the Sabbath school's Superintendent Jas. F. Turner and Secretary pro tem Josiah Allen [VERIFY]; also signed Mary D. Weaks [VERIFY].
people: deceased; teacher, A.M.E. Union Church Sabbath school
Superintendent, A.M.E. Union Church Sabbath school

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: In this city (Philadelphia), on the 12th inst., by Rev. Peter Gardiner, Mr. Wm. Reed, of Reading, Pa., to Mrs. Susan Gibson, of the Eastern Shore of Maryland. Also: in Trinity Church, Monrovia, Liberia, Feb. 25, by Rev. G. W. Gibson, Mr. William M. Davis to Miss Jane Frances L. Sherman, both of Monrovia (non-Philadelphia).

articles.headline: Ice Cream Saloon -- Mrs. J. [surname illegible] (new advertisement)
articles.summary: Mrs. J. [surname VERIFY] has lately opened an ice cream saloon at No. [9?]13 Lombard Street [VERIFY], Philadelphia, for the accommodation of ladies and gentlemen, and hopes to share the patronage of her friends; she will also supply families. Dated June 16 (3m) -- a new standing ad. Proprietor's surname and the street number are obscured by paper bleed-through and could not be read with confidence.

articles.headline: Zollickoffer's Anti-Rheumatic Cordial (new advertisement/endorsement)
articles.author: E. Weaver
articles.summary: Endorsement notice: 'Rheumatism can be cured' -- announcing to readers of the Recorder that Mr. Zollickoffer's Anti-Rheumatic Cordial will cure rheumatism if taken as directed; a cure claimed after half a bottle. Only $1.00 per bottle. Signed E. Weaver.

articles.headline: Protest against the Sunday School flag award (J. W. Cromwell)
articles.summary: A protest against the decision of the committee to award the Sunday School flag (the missionary flag given at the June A.M.E. Sabbath School anniversary) has been entered by J. W. Cromwell, late a teacher in the Bethel [VERIFY] Church Sabbath school.
people: entered the protest; late a teacher in the Bethel Church Sabbath school

articles.headline: An Acknowledgment (Excelsior Base Ball Club of Philadelphia)
articles.summary: The members of the Excelsior Base Ball Club of Philadelphia express appreciation of the action of their friends, whose liberality secured for them the set of implements voted for at the late fair of the Ladies' Union Association (of the Shiloh Baptist church), and thank their lady friends who wore the club's colors. They resolve to take 'nulla vestigia retrorsum' (no steps backward). Signed James H. Francis, President; J. Fields Needham, Secretary.

articles.headline: Personal Items
articles.summary: The New York Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church met at Sullivan St. Church last Wednesday, Bishop A. W. Wayman presiding, assisted by Bishop Payne. Rumor that the trustees of the African M.E. Church, Brooklyn, seek Rev. James Morris Williams (present pastor) as financial agent to liquidate an $8,000 debt. Bishop D. A. Payne passed through Philadelphia last week en route to Conference. Business manager of Zion's Standard and Weekly Review visited Philadelphia. (Chiefly non-Philadelphia except Payne's passage through the city.)
people: passed through Philadelphia en route to Conference (Bishop)

articles.headline: Colored Schools in Pennsylvania (Commissioners' Report)
articles.author: P. H. C.
articles.summary: Editorial (signed P. H. C.) on the Pennsylvania school law and the State Superintendent's Commissioners' Report: of 625 districts containing colored youth of school age, only 171 enumerate more than twenty, and in most townships colored youth are too widely scattered to attend separate schools; argues the Boards' refusal to admit colored children to the common schools is a mockery (six weeks of schooling for colored youth against twenty-six for white). References work for the Equal Rights League. Promises more extracts from the Commissioners' Report.

articles.headline: In Memoriam (deceased ministers, from the Minutes of the Philadelphia Annual Conference)
articles.summary: Memorial from the Minutes of the recent session of the Philadelphia Annual Conference. Rev. Thomas H. Cooper (b. Baltimore; joined the A.M.E. Church and removed to Pennsylvania; admitted on trial to the Philadelphia Conference 1861; ordained Deacon by Bishop Nazrey 1863 and appointed to the Philadelphia Mission, then Trenton; ordained Elder by Bishop Wayman 1865; died of consumption, in great peace, April 23, 1866). Rev. Geo. McMullen (b. Albany, N.Y.; licensed to preach 1830 by 'our late father Rev. Richard Robertson'; died, deeply felt by the citizens of Trenton). Rev. Shepherd Holcomb (son of Richard and Beulah Holcomb, b. Princeton, N.J., 1806; Presbyterian then Methodist; superannuated after paralysis; died January). Rev. Andrew Massey (b. Baltimore county, Md.; went to Delaware then Philadelphia, and after forming an acquaintance with Bishop Richard Allen joined the Philadelphia Annual Conference; died aged 110 [VERIFY]). Rev. Robert Reeves (b. Delaware; raised in a Quaker family named Reeves near Medford, N.J.; a pioneer and one of the founders of the A.M.E. Church, establishing several churches in N.J. and Pennsylvania).
people: deceased; Philadelphia Conference minister who knew Bishop Richard Allen (Rev.)
deceased; A.M.E. pioneer in N.J. and Pennsylvania (Rev.)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting / Quarterly Conference notices (Philadelphia Conference charges)
articles.summary: Cluster of Philadelphia Conference notices: Quarterly Conference of Bethel A.M.E. Church, Philadelphia, Tuesday July 17 (Quarterly Meeting the 22d), James Hollen, Minister; Quarterly Meetings at Horntown (June 30/July 1), Chester (July 7/8), Chichester (July 15/16), Jeremiah Young, Minister; Quarterly Conference at Gouldtown, N.J. (June 30), Jos. A. Nelson, Pastor; Burlington Circuit -- Evesham (July 8), Mount Holly (July 15), Burlington (July 22), Jacob Mitchell, Minister in charge; Mount Zion M.E. Church (Trenton), July 7/8, William Moore, Pastor; First Quarterly Meeting in Wesley A.M.E. Church, on Hurst street (Little Wesley), Sunday July 15, Wm. M. Watson, Pastor (also notice to the Annual Conference members that Wm. M. Watson, District Steward, holds the Minutes at 15 cents); Quarterly Meeting of the West Philadelphia Circuit at Norristown (July 15) and Germantown (Conference; Meeting July 23); Chester Co. circuit -- Great Valley (July 7/8), Phoenixville (July 14/15), Downingtown (July 21/22), James Jones, Deacon in Charge, W. R. Norris, Elder; and Rev. James Lynch to preach at the A.M.E. Church, Salem, N.J., Sunday July 1.
people: Pastor, Wesley A.M.E. (Hurst St./Little Wesley); District Steward (Rev.)

articles.headline: Personal Items
articles.summary: Bishop William Paul Quinn left New York for his home in Richmond, Ind., having held the New England Annual Conference. Bishop D. A. Payne left Philadelphia on Saturday for Wilberforce University. Rev. B. T. Tanner, of Baltimore, visited the office. (Other items -- an engraver named Reason and the Treasurer of the Liberian Republic -- are in New York.)
people: left New York for Richmond, Ind. (Bishop)

articles.headline: Ill-Treatment of Patrons (Upham's Confectionery and Ice Cream Saloon)
articles.author: A. P.
articles.summary: A colored patron recounts being refused service in a recess of Upham's Confectionery and Ice Cream Saloon, on Pine Street between Sixth and Seventh (a white-owned establishment that enjoys considerable patronage from colored people); told he could not eat there. He urges colored people not to spend money where they are 'less esteemed than dogs' and to patronize the confectionery and ice cream saloons kept by colored men instead. Signed A. P.

articles.headline: Excelsior Base Ball Club -- Fall tour
articles.summary: The Excelsior Base Ball Club of Philadelphia, comprising some of the first, best and most intelligent young gentlemen, is making extensive arrangements to visit New York, Baltimore and Washington city this Fall, to establish a more perfect union among these cities in playing the game of base ball.

articles.headline: Major Martin R. Delany, U.S.C.T. (appointment at Hilton Head)
articles.summary: Notes General Orders No. 6, Headquarters U.S. Forces, Charleston, S.C., announcing the Sub-District of Hilton Head (Hilton Head, Daufuskie, Bull and Pinckney Islands) with Major M. R. Delany, U.S.C.T., as Sub-Assistant Commissioner in charge (Freedmen's Bureau), headquarters at Hilton Head. Observes that Delany, the only colored field officer mustered into the U.S. service, retained in service by special order of the War Department, so enjoys the confidence of the Government that he holds a Freedmen's Bureau post. (Concerns his South Carolina post; non-Philadelphia.)

events.name: Order 'Light and Truth' (O. R. E. C.) -- entertainment at the African Union Church
events.description: An entertainment given by the order of 'Light and Truth' (initials printed O. R. E. C. [VERIFY]) on Wednesday evening, Feb. 28, at the African Union Church, 30th St. Interesting addresses by male members of the order and singing of popular operatic airs by Miss Julie Thompson, Miss Henry and other vocalists. The order's Master, G. V. Peterson, delivered a speech on the order's principles ('Light and Truth'), the order having been organized a month before; motto 'Light and Truth.' A committee of ladies sold cream, cakes and mottoes. Persons wishing to communicate may address Geo. Simmons, G. S., 110 (--) 30th St. A new benevolent/fraternal order of both male and female members, similar to the order of Love and Charity. Society / lodge topic.

events.name: Grand Semi-Centenary Meeting -- Bethel A.M.E. Church (laymen)
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth street above Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: The laymen of Bethel A.M.E. church will hold a grand semi-centenary meeting at the church, Sixth street above Lombard, on Thursday evening, April 12th; exercises of singing and historical mention of church incidents by the old members and others, with a thanksgiving-offering. Committee of Arrangements: Abm. Fields, Henry Gordon, Rev. J. P. B. Eddy, Wm. Scott, Lewis R. Seymour. A.M.E. Semi-Centenary topic.

events.name: Semi-Centenary Rally -- Union A.M.E. Church
events.location: Union Church, Philadelphia (Rev. R. P. Gibbs, pastor)
events.description: A Semi-Centenary Rally at the Union church of this city (Rev. R. P. Gibbs, pastor) on Sabbath, April 15th: 11 A.M. (speaker not named in notice); 3 P.M. Rev. Jas. Lynch; 7.30 P.M. Bishop Wayman. A.M.E. Semi-Centenary topic.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at Frankford
events.description: Notice: Rev. J. H. Smith will hold his quarterly meeting at Frankford, Pa., on the fourth Sabbath in April; friends invited.

events.name: Grand Fair -- Union Baptist Sabbath School
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Minster Street above Sixth, Philadelphia
events.description: A Grand Fair for the sale of useful and fancy articles, given at the Union Baptist Sabbath School for its benefit, at the Union Baptist Church, Minster Street above Sixth, beginning Easter Monday evening, April 2, 1866, continuing through the week. Object: to buy a new set of books and library for the school, the present set to be given to the Freedmen. Tickets 10 cts (single), 25 cts (season); to be had of the teachers or scholars. No individual names printed.

events.name: Semi-Centenary sermon -- Bethel Church, Baltimore
events.description: Notice: Rev. Jas. Lynch (editor of the Christian Recorder) will preach the semi-centenary sermon in Bethel church, Baltimore, next Sabbath, the 8th inst., at 3 o'clock P.M. Out-of-area location; recorded for the Semi-Centenary topic and Lynch's editorship.

events.name: Garnet League lecture -- Rev. James Lynch at Harrisburg
events.description: Notice: Rev. James Lynch will lecture before the Garnet League, at Harrisburg, Pa., Thursday evening next, 19th inst. Subject -- 'Our Movement on the Track.' Tickets of T. Morris Chester, Esq., and A. T. Haunt [VERIFY] (Harrisburg agents, out of area). Equal Rights / suffrage-movement topic (the Garnet League was a Harrisburg colored equal-rights organization).

events.name: Banneker Institute lecture -- Hon. John W. Forney at Concert Hall
events.description: Notice: The Hon. John W. Forney (white journalist) will lecture before the Banneker Institute at Concert Hall on Thursday evening, April 19th. Subject -- 'Has the war for Human Freedom been fought in vain?' Tickets 35 cents, for sale at Pugh's (Sixth and Chestnut), Trumpler's (Seventh and Chestnut), and by members of the Institute. Banneker Institute topic (Philadelphia colored literary society).

events.name: Semi-Centenary services -- Little Wesley Church (Hurst St.)
events.location: Little Wesley Church, Hurst St., Philadelphia
events.description: Semi-Centenary services at Little Wesley Church, Hurst St., on Sunday next, 15th inst.: 11 A.M. Rev. Jacob Mitchell; 3 P.M. Bishop A. W. Wayman. A.M.E. Semi-Centenary topic (Hurst St. Wesley = Little Wesley, A.M.E.).

events.name: Semi-Centenary Anniversary -- Bethel Church
events.location: Bethel Church, South Sixth Street below Pine Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Semi-Centenary Anniversary services at Bethel Church, South Sixth Street below Pine Street, next Sabbath, April 15th: preaching 10 A.M. by Rt. Rev. A. W. Wayman; 3 P.M. Rev. Wm. Moore; 7.30 P.M. Rev. James Lynch. Friends of 'Old Bethel' urged to the special semi-centennial collection. A.M.E. Semi-Centenary topic.

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School Semi-Centennial Celebration
events.description: On Monday evening, April 16th, at Bethel Church, the Sabbath-school will celebrate the Semi-centennial of the A.M.E. Church; the school has long ranked high in the Philadelphia Conference for contributions to the Mission fund. Admission ten cents. Addresses by Rev. Jas. Lynch and others. A.M.E. Semi-Centenary topic.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association (SCSA) -- universal-suffrage fund
events.location: Rooms of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia
events.description: At a meeting of the Executive Committee of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania, held at their Rooms, April 2, 1866, a resolution empowered Messrs. Wm. Still, J. C. White, Sr., and U. B. Vidom [VERIFY = Vidal?] to raise $1,000 for the Union Congressional Committee, to circulate speeches and documents in favor of universal suffrage. President read as 'J. O. Weaas' [VERIFY, prob. I. C. Wears]; Secretary J. C. White. The acknowledged donations ('Colored Men Distributing Loyal Publications'): the Association itself $100; at $50 -- Stephen Smith, Wm. Still, Jno. W. Price, James Hester, Thos. J. Dorsey, Ladies' Sanitary Assoc. of St. Thomas' Church; at $25 -- James Prosser, Wm. Whipper; at $20 -- Henry Jones and Mrs. S. Townsend, Mrs. Savage; at $10 -- Henry Minton, J. Augustin, Robert Adger, J. C. White Sr., John Shaw, Clayton Miller, R. T. Tompkins, J. W. Page, Wm. G. Freeman, Henry Gordon, U. B. Vidom, Daniel George, Lewis R. Seymour, Samuel Roberts, Augusta Dorsey, (T.) Francis, Jas. P. Clay, H. Shedd, Isaiah Hinkson, John Magee, Thomas H. Lewis, Lewis Alexander, Levi Cromwell, Wm. Scott, Peter Lewis, Theo. Young, Mrs. Sarah Newman; Henry Smith $8; at $5 -- George W. Woolford, J. Whipper Purnell, Thomas Charnock, James Bustill, Henry Hernue, Franklin Turner, J. Downs, R. H. Gleaves, J. T. Robinson, Mrs. S. B. Hankins, Hartwell Shands, W. A. Ready, Mrs. & Miss White, S. Coleman, Isaac Foster, Abraham Field, Theo. Coonte, Edward Green, Mrs. Lucy Du(terte?), W. H. Reilly, J. C. Wears, Chas. Simpson, Wm. T. Simpson, Mrs. C. Simpson, Mrs. Belinda Jackson, J. C. Green, Edward Collins, Robt. Wilson, Rev. Wm. Moore, A. Lawrence, J. W. Adams, James Alexander, L. Brown, Morris Brown, J. Dixon, Mr. Campbell, J. H. Moore; collected by John C. Bowers -- John C. Bowers $10, Stephen Purnell $5, Ellis Peer $1, Wm. Brandt $1, David Trout 50c. Sum total $1,010.50, forwarded to the Union Congressional Finance Committee. With Banneker Institute $100 (and $121 collected = $221) and the Ladies' Union Association $40, grand total $1,281.50, transmitted to Washington. Committee: Wm. Still, Jacob C. White, Sr., U. B. Vidom. EQUAL RIGHTS / suffrage topic. (Full donor list in text; a curated set of clearly-read, distinctive names linked.)

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference (spring 1866) -- notice and candidate classes
events.description: Notice to the members of the Philadelphia Conference of the A.M.E. Church (signed A. W. Wayman, Baltimore, March 28, 1866): the Annual Meeting will convene at Princeton, New Jersey -- a place where the Conference has never before met -- on Wednesday, May 23d. Candidate classes named: First year -- R. Faucet, Wm. H. Turner, Harrison Lewis; Second year -- Wm. R. Norris, James V. Pearce; Third year -- Joseph A. Nelson; Fourth year -- Thomas A. Creff, Jacob P. Jay, Edward Laws, John W. Stevenson, Gilbert Waters, Daniel P. Seaton. Rev. Wm. M. Watson replaces Rev. James M. Williams on the third-year committee. The Annual sermon to be preached by Rev. Wm. Moore (May 23, 3 P.M.); the Missionary sermon Friday the 25th by Rev. A. C. Crippen; the (Semi-)Centenary sermon Monday the 27th/28th by Rev. Joseph H. Smith. Philadelphia Annual Conference / Semi-Centenary topic.

events.name: Lecture by Mrs. F. E. W. Harper -- 'Home Influence'
events.location: First Presbyterian Church, South Seventh street below Shippen, Philadelphia
events.description: Mrs. F. E. W. Harper will lecture at the First Presbyterian Church, South Seventh street below Shippen, next Thursday evening (May 3), subject 'Home Influence.' She has been well received in various cities this season; Philadelphians will recall her earlier lecture 'the Nation's Great Opportunity' before the Social, Civil and Statistical Association. Tickets 25 cents, at the office of the Christian Recorder.

events.name: Fourth Quarterly Meeting -- Little Wesley (Wesley Church, Hurst St.)
events.description: Jacob M. Mitchell's notice: on Sabbath, May 6, his fourth and last Quarterly Meeting at Wesley Church, Hurst St. (Little Wesley). Preaching in the morning by Rev. H. J. Rhodes, in the afternoon by Rev. Mr. Brown of the M.E. Church; 'some of the best talent in the city.'

events.name: Quarterly Meeting -- Germantown A.M.E. Church
events.description: By divine permission, Quarterly Meeting at the A.M.E. Church, Germantown, Pa., on the last Sabbath in April (29th). H. J. Rhodes, Minister in charge.

events.name: Fourth Quarterly Meeting -- Princeton Circuit
events.location: Little Rocky Hill (Apr 29) and Princeton, N.J. (May 6)
events.description: The Fourth Quarterly Meeting of the Princeton Circuit: April 29 at Little Rocky Hill; May 6 at Princeton. Rev. N. H. Turpin and other invited ministers to be present at Princeton. J. B. Hamilton, Minister in charge.

events.name: Fourth Quarterly Conference/Meeting -- Chester Circuit
events.description: Peter Gardiner's notice: Saturday the 28th, his fourth and last Quarterly Conference at Chester, 8 P.M.; Sunday the 29th, Quarterly Meeting. Peter Gardiner, Preacher in charge of Chester Circuit.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference -- 1866 spring session (meeting notice)
events.description: Editorial notice (Meeting of Annual Conferences): the Philadelphia Conference will meet on the 23d inst. at Princeton, New Jersey; Bishop Wayman will preside and Bishops Quinn and Campbell are expected to be present. (Same notice states Bishop Payne's South Carolina Conference will meet at Savannah, Ga., on the 12th inst.)

events.name: Ladies' Fair at Masonic Hall (to aid the Christian Recorder)
events.description: The Ladies' Fair at Masonic Hall, held to aid the Christian Recorder, opened on Tuesday, May 1, 1866; attendance good despite an unfavorable night. A fine silver pitcher was to be presented to the Philadelphia minister receiving the highest vote. No individual ladies named in the notice. Signed Elisha Weaver, Publisher.

events.name: Bethel Sunday School -- Sabbath address (notice)
events.description: Notice that next Sabbath the Bethel Sunday School of Philadelphia will be addressed by the pastor and several other brethren at 3 P.M.; parents and friends invited. The pastor is not named in the notice (Bethel's pastor this period is Rev. William Moore).

events.name: Wesley Church (Hurst Street, Little Wesley) -- Fourth Quarterly Conference
events.description: Notice: at Wesley church, Hurst street, on Sabbath May 6th, the fourth Quarterly Conference will be held. Preaching in the morning by Rev. H. J. Rhodes; in the afternoon by Rev. Mr. Brown of the M.E. Church; in the evening by Rev. Mr. Homer. Signed Jacob M. Mitchell, April 28, 1866 (the pastor). Hurst Street Wesley = Little Wesley (A.M.E.) per owner's ruling.

events.name: Semi-Centenary of the A.M.E. Church -- Burlington N.J. circuit observance
events.location: Burlington, Mount Holly and Evesham, New Jersey
events.description: Letter from Burlington, N.J. (signed T. Gould, dated April 24, 1866): the circuit celebrated the semi-centenary of the A.M.E. Church. Semi-centenary collections reported: Burlington Church $16.85 and Sabbath-school $24.07 (making $40.42); Mount Holly Church $15.70 and Sabbath-school $2.93; Evesham Church $5; total about $64.05. A protracted meeting at Evesham added 52 souls. The last quarterly meeting to be held at Burlington on Sabbath, May 6th, with a general invitation to friends in Philadelphia. (Burlington is a N.J. circuit of the Philadelphia Conference.)

events.name: A.M.E. Church dedication at Millville, N.J.
events.description: Personal Items: Bishop A. W. Wayman, accompanied by Rev. Stephen Smith, dedicated the A.M.E. Church at Millville on Sunday last (about May 6, 1866); reported a snug building reflecting credit on the denomination in that vicinity. (Millville is in the Philadelphia Conference's New Jersey territory.)

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League officers in Philadelphia
events.description: Personal Items: W. C. Nennit, Esq. [VERIFY], President, and Mr. O. C. L. Hughes [VERIFY], Secretary, of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, have been in Philadelphia ('our city') this week. events.name: A.M.E. Zion Philadelphia Annual Conference (at Big Wesley / Wesley Church, Lombard St.)
events.description: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Zion Church in America met in Wesley church, Lombard street (Big Wesley / First Colored Wesley), on the 5th instant at 4 o'clock P.M., Superintendent John Brooks presiding, assisted by Superintendent William H. Bishop. Letters read from Superintendent J. J. Clinton and Elder S. M. Giles (Baltimore Conf.) on Missions, and from Elder Wm. F. Butler on a connexional organ. A circular from New York announced a paper, 'The Zion Standard and Weekly Review,' to issue about June 15 (M. B. Coss, Business Manager, Box 6164, New York). A Board of Missions was organized: Elder D. Stevens chairman, S. G. Golder corresponding secretary. Elder J. S. Wilson restored to membership; the cases of Elders H. H. Blackiston and Wm. Young left with the Superintendents; Chester Maddix transferred to the Baltimore Conference. Delegates elected to other Annual Conferences: Geo. Bosley (New York), D. Stevens (Baltimore), S. G. Golder (New England), Thomas H. Biddle (Genesee), J. P. Hamer (Kentucky), Thomas H. Harris (North Carolina). Next session at York, Pa., first Saturday in May 1867. Benediction by Elder S. T. Scott; signed J. P. Hamer, Secretary. (A.M.E. Zion connexional ministers; recorded in the description, not linked, as their Philadelphia residence is not established.)

events.name: Shiloh Baptist Church -- public recognition of Rev. Chauncey Leonard as pastor
events.location: Shiloh Baptist Church, corner Clifton and South Streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Public recognition services installing Rev. Chauncey Leonard as pastor of the Shiloh Baptist Church, corner of Clifton and South Streets, Philadelphia, held Thursday evening, May 3, 1866, at quarter before 8 o'clock. Order of services: hymn by Rev. James Underdue, pastor of Union Baptist Church, Philadelphia; reading of Scriptures by Rev. J. Newton Brown, D.D.; prayer by Rev. Samuel W. Madden, pastor of First Baptist Church, Alexandria, Va.; selection by the choir; sermon by Rev. Reuben Jeffery, D.D., pastor of Fourth Baptist Church, Phila.; prayer by Rev. D. W. Anderson, pastor of First Baptist Church, Washington, D.C.; the recognition itself by Rev. James H. Simmons, pastor of Fifth Baptist Church, Philadelphia; closing by the choir and benediction. (Jeffery, Simmons and J. Newton Brown appear to be white assisting ministers; the Black Philadelphia Baptist figures are Leonard and Underdue.)
attendees: installed as pastor, Shiloh Baptist Church (Rev.)
pastor of Union Baptist Church, Philadelphia (Rev.)

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth -- resolutions on the death of Francis M. Seymour
events.description: At a special meeting of the Senior and Middle classes of the Institute for Colored Youth, on the 7th inst., preamble and resolutions were unanimously adopted on the death of their fellow-student Francis M. Seymour, praising his character and zeal in his studies and condoling with his father and family. Signed: Horace F. Owens, President; Frazelia Campbell, Secretary; F. D. Minton; John H. Davis; Henry J. Locke; Hester A. Glasgow; Sarah L. Iredell, Committee.

events.name: Bethel Church -- examination of the fourth year's class (notice)
events.location: Bethel Church (Elder's study), South Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: the fourth year's class, to be examined -- Daniel Weston, Gilbert Waters, John W. Stevenson, Jacob C. Joy, Edward Laws and Thomas A. Hall -- requested to meet in the Elder's study at Bethel Church on Monday morning, the 21st inst., at 9 o'clock. Committee: Peter Gardiner, Wm. Moore, Joseph H. Smith, John Henson.

events.name: Macedonia A.M.E. Church -- grand rally
events.description: Notice: the trustees and minister of the A.M.E. Macedonia Church intend a grand rally on Sunday, May 27, hoping to raise two hundred dollars to clear the entire church property of debt. One or more of the bishops and members of Conference expected; the choirs of Bethel, Union and Little Wesley A.M.E. Churches invited. No individual names given (trustees/minister unnamed).

events.location: Union Church, Coates St. below Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: Rev. T. D. Miller, pastor of Pearl Street Baptist Church, will deliver his celebrated lecture on 'Love' at Union Church, Coates St. below Fifth Street, on May 22d; proceeds for the benefit of the Union Sabbath School. Signed W. H. Davis.
attendees: lecturer, pastor of Pearl Street Baptist Church (Rev.)

events.name: Pearl Street Baptist Church Sabbath School -- grand concert
events.description: Notice: a grand concert by the Sabbath school of the Pearl Street Baptist Church, Thursday evening, May 24, 1866, at Sansom Street Hall; Rev. T. D. Miller to deliver an address. Admission 30 cents.

events.name: Philadelphia Conference Sabbath-school anniversary (at Bethel)
events.location: Bethel Church, South Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Special Notice: the anniversary of the Philadelphia Conference Sabbath school will take place in Bethel Church, South Sixth Street, Philadelphia, on Monday afternoon, June 4, 1866; superintendents of participating schools asked to have their scholars at the church in proper time. Signed A. W. Wayman, Baltimore, May 12, 1866.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church (spring 1866 session)
events.location: Princeton, New Jersey (met in the colored Presbyterian church)
events.description: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church met at Princeton, N.J., Wednesday May 23 and adjourned Monday night May 28, 1866. Bishop A. W. Wayman presided, assisted by Bishop J. P. Campbell. Rev. H. J. Rhodes elected Secretary, Rev. R. P. Gibbs Assistant. No reporter was appointed, so full proceedings were not printed. Reports from circuits/stations showed a prosperous condition; Semi-Centenary collections throughout the District reported over $2,000 (Semi-Centenary watch topic). Rev. Jos. A. Nelson was complained of and exonerated. Rev. John M. Brown, Corresponding Secretary of the Parent Home & Foreign Missionary Society (just elected by the General Conference to that office), addressed the Conference on missions. Rev. J. A. Shorter, Agent of Wilberforce University, also addressed it. Rev. James Lynch, editor of the Christian Recorder, was declared a member of the Conference. Bishop Campbell preached at the ordination of Deacons, Bishop Wayman at that of Elders. Rev. William Moore (former pastor of Bethel Church, Philadelphia) preached the sermon to the Daughters of Conference, Tuesday evening. A p2 editorial adds statistics: 37 traveling and 118 local preachers, membership not less than 17,000, about 120 churches valued over $[...], Sunday-schools with 8,910 scholars and nearly 12,000 library volumes. APPOINTMENTS (36 charges) as printed: Bethel Church -- James Hollen, J. G. [surname VERIFY] superannuated; Union Bethel Church -- Richard Gibbs; Wesley Church -- W. M. Watson; Salem, N.J. -- Nelson H. Turpin; Trenton, N.J. -- Wm. Moore; Zion Church, Phila. -- Theodore Gould; New Brunswick -- Benjamin Lynch; Camden Station -- George E. Chase; West Chester -- James V. Pearce; Smyrna -- G. Draper; Camden -- G. Waters; Frederica -- J. S. Taylor; Vineland -- Thomas Pierce; Pennington Mission -- to be supplied; Oaklawn -- Jas. A. Nelson; Philadelphia City Mission -- to be supplied; Massalpee Mission -- Lewis Conner [VERIFY]; Laurel -- John H. Hanson; Milton -- Harrison H. Lewis [VERIFY]. James Lynch named a member of Bethel Church Quarterly Conference; E. Weaver (General Book Steward) a member of Union Bethel Church Quarterly Conference.
attendees: Corresponding Secretary, Parent Home & Foreign Missionary Society (Rev.)

events.description: Notice of the [semi-annual] meeting of District Grand Lodge No. 2, I.O. of G.S. and D.S. (Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria), to be held at the Masonic Hall, Eleventh Street, Tuesday morning, June 5th, at 10 o'clock A.M. By order of the W.G.C. Attest, W. A. R. Smith, D.G.R.S. (District Grand Recording Secretary).

events.name: A.M.E. Sabbath School Anniversary (Philadelphia)
events.description: On Monday of this week the anniversary celebration of the Sabbath Schools of the city was held, well attended, at Bethel Church. Three schools were present -- the Bethel, Union and Zion Mission Sabbath Schools -- each singing a chorus after the addresses. Speeches were made by Rev. Messrs. Smith, Marship [VERIFY] and Seaton, and by Mr. W. E. Matthews, of Baltimore. A missionary (silk) flag was presented by Dr. Wm. Armstrong, of the M.E. Church, to the Union Sabbath School, as the school raising the largest amount of missionary money during the Conference year (Dr. Armstrong had promised it at the 1865 anniversary); the friends of the Zion school claimed the flag should have gone to that school owing to a reporting error.
attendees: presented the missionary flag to the Union Sabbath School (Dr.; M.E. Church)

events.name: Missionary Society of the Philadelphia Conference -- anniversary
events.description: The anniversary of the Missionary Society of the Philadelphia Conference took place at Bethel Church on Tuesday evening. Attendance was smaller than the occasion demanded. Rev. Stephen Smith presided; Rev. E. Weaver read the Annual Report. Addresses were delivered by Bishop Campbell, Rev. John M. Brown (Missionary Secretary), Rev. J. Walker Jackson and Alfred Cookman of the Methodist Episcopal Church. John M. Brown gave an account of the progress of missions; Bishop Campbell spoke of the necessities of the missionaries to the South-west. John Walker Jackson said his brother was a colonel of the colored regiment massacred at Fort Pillow and that he (Jackson) had made the first speech in Philadelphia in behalf of arming colored men during the civil war.

events.name: William Moore's farewell sermon at Bethel Church
events.description: William Moore, the former pastor of Bethel church, preached his farewell sermon last Sabbath afternoon (text: Acts xx.32), touching on the peace and harmony during his administration, the souls converted, and his long service, and giving advice to the classes of persons in the congregation. At the close, Rev. Stephen Smith arose and paid a high tribute to the worth of the late pastor and invited the congregation to show appreciation by a contribution; in a few minutes they presented Moore with seventy dollars.
attendees: retiring pastor who preached his farewell (Rev.)
paid tribute and moved the contribution (Rev.)

events.name: Sacred concert by the Caroline Twins (Millie and Christine), Union A.M.E. Church
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Notice ('Come one! Come all!') of a sacred concert by the Caroline Twins, Millie and Christine, at the Union A.M.E. Church, Coates Street, Tuesday night the 19th, a portion of the proceeds for the benefit of the church. The faculty of Jefferson College of the city had examined the children; after the concert the audience could converse with and test the educational knowledge of Millie and Christine. Admission 25 cts., children 15 cts.; doors open 7, concert at 8. Thomas T. Simpson, Chairman of Committee.

events.name: Zion Mission A.M.E. Church -- First Quarterly Meeting
events.location: Zion Mission A.M.E. Church, 7th below Dickerson St., Philadelphia
events.description: The First Quarterly Meeting of Zion Mission A.M.E. Church, 7th below Dickerson St., Philadelphia, to be held Sabbath, July 8, 1866. Appointments: Sabbath morning 10:30, Rev. J. Hollen; afternoon 3:00, Rev. J. Lynch; evening 8:00, Rev. J. H. Smith. 'Come to the Mission and help us.' Theodore Gould, Pastor.

events.name: Fair in aid of the Book Room (A.M.E. Book Concern)
events.location: Masonic Hall, Philadelphia; presentation at 619 Pine Street
events.description: Early last spring Rev. Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward, enlisted several ladies to get up a fair for the benefit of the Book Concern; they opened at Masonic Hall early in May, holding it a little over two weeks. A silver pitcher was procured and all the city's ministers enrolled as competitors to be voted for; Weaver, as the successful competitor, was presented the pitcher on Tuesday evening, June 12, at his residence, 619 Pine Street, by the ladies of the Fair through Miss Georgiana R. Matthiat, who also presented the proceeds, $100. Committee of Arrangements: Mrs. Charles Givens, Mrs. Sophia A. Woolard, Mrs. Frances G. Boston, Miss Elizabeth Douglass, Miss Sarah Chandler, Mrs. Eliza Stokely. Officers: Mrs. J. D. Matthiat, President; Miss Georgiana R. Matthiat, Secretary; Miss Mary F. Hartley [VERIFY], Assistant Secretary; Miss M. Oakey, Treasurer.

events.name: Fair of the Ladies' Union Association of the Shiloh Baptist Church (base ball prize)
events.description: The Ladies' Union Association of the Shiloh Baptist church closed a Fair at Masonic Hall with large attendance. Among the articles contested was a fine set of base ball club equipments, hotly contested for by the Independence and Excelsior clubs and won by the Excelsior club. Also a silver cup and pitcher to be presented by vote to the pastor of the Union, Shiloh, or Pearl St. churches; the pastor of the Pearl St. church, Rev. T. D. Miller, having the most votes, was awarded the pitcher. The Association is composed entirely of the young.
attendees: pastor of the Pearl St. (Baptist) church; awarded the pitcher (Rev.)

events.name: Freedmen's Fair (Freedmen's Aid Society of Philadelphia)
events.location: the New Hall, Lombard Street above Seventh, Philadelphia (formerly the Institute for Colored Youth)
events.description: A Freedmen's Fair, held by the Freedmen's Aid Society of Philadelphia for the benefit of the Freedmen, opening the new hall on Lombard Street (formerly the Institute for Colored Youth), on the evenings of July 1, 2 and 3 and the morning of the 4th (p3 notice gives the evenings of the 2d and 3d and the morning of the 4th, at 10 o'clock). Season tickets 25 cents; single admission 15 cents; children 10 cents.
